body.text: In normal operation, the RPS keeps voltage on the RTB undervoltage coils, which holds RTBs closed.
body.anchor: the RPS maintains voltage on the RTB undervoltage coils to keep RTBs in the closed position

body.text: Closed RTBs keep power on CRD solenoid valve coils, which keep argon pressure to hold the rods.
body.anchor: maintaining power to the CRD solenoid operated valve coils

body.text: On loss of incoming power, RTBs open, CRD argon vents, and rods drop by gravity.
body.anchor: venting CRD argon and allowing rods to drop fully into the core via gravity

body.text: ESF circuits also de-energize to trip. On loss of power, relay contacts open and pump breakers trip.
body.anchor: tripping the pump breakers, and stopping pump rotation

body.text: On a critical fault found by self-diagnostics, the system places all outputs in the safe, tripped state.
body.anchor: the system places all outputs to the safe (tripped) state

body.text: Range-checking detects loss of power at a transmitting system, and the RPS places the associated outputs in the safe state.
body.anchor: loss of power at the transmitting system is detected by RPS range-checking

body.text: Once started, the sequence of protective actions continues to completion. Deliberate operator action is required to return the RPS to normal.

title: Reactor Protection System
subject: RPS
intro: The RPS is the safety-related logic that scrams the reactor and trips pumps. Four divisions, two-out-of-four voting, and de-energize to trip are the three ideas to master.

objectives.text: State the purpose of the RPS.
Identify the RPS boundaries and interfaces.
Identify the major components of the RPS.
Describe the RPS controls and indications.
Explain the RPS automatic features and interlocks.
Apply operating procedures for the RPS.
Diagnose abnormal conditions in the RPS.
Explain the safety significance of the RPS.
Address technical specifications and administrative controls for the RPS.
